kpis.sub: XI'S WASHINGTON SUMMIT WRAPS WITH NO REAL CHANGE TO CHINA'S EXPORT REGIME (SEP 24-25)
kpis.label: Xi Jinping's first White House visit in 11 years produced tariff cuts on ~$30B of goods and a new trade committee, but on rare earths the two sides couldn't even agree on what happened: the White House cited a softer commitment from Beijing to 'address concerns' over yttrium, scandium and NdPr shortages, while China's own 8-point summit readout omitted rare earths entirely. April 2025's export-licensing regime stands unchanged, and Washington's prior demand that China 'eliminate' the controls has quietly been dropped. MP Materials closed Sep 25 at $48.83, still 31% off its August high — also sits in the Robotics sleeve, don't double-count

kpis.sub: CHINA'S RARE-EARTH MAGNET SHIPMENTS TO THE US KEEP SHRINKING (AUG DATA, REPORTED SEP 21)
kpis.label: Chinese rare-earth magnet exports to the US fell to just 512 tonnes in August — down 20% from July and 13% year-over-year — even as the Trump-Xi summit approached. Capital Economics says Beijing 'appears willing to test the limits of the truce,' deliberately keeping licence approvals 'slow and selective,' while some Chinese suppliers are independently withholding shipments out of fear of Beijing retaliation

kpis.sub: LITHIUM CARBONATE SNAPS ITS MONTH-LONG SLIDE ON CHINA EV RESTOCKING (SEP 22)
kpis.label: Battery-grade lithium carbonate bounced to roughly $20,010/tonne as Chinese battery makers restocked chemicals ahead of year-end production, reversing a month of declines — Albemarle rose 1.8% to $112.92 and SQM jumped 2.7% the same day. Analysts frame this as normalization, not a new bull leg: prices are still down ~12% from May's $27,000/t peak, which one analyst called a rally that had 'outrun market fundamentals'

kpis.sub: COPPER HITS A FRESH RECORD ON AI DATA-CENTER DEMAND (SEP 22-23)
kpis.label: Copper set a new all-time high as AI data centers become a major source of demand, global mine supply falls behind, US tariff-driven stockpiling redirects inventory, and China's own copper demand shows signs of recovery. Freeport closed at $72.31 with its market cap up 92% year-over-year to $103.8B — right at the Street's $72.45 average price target, leaving little obvious room for the record price to re-rate the stock further

themes.title: Xi's Washington visit produced a trade truce but no rare-earth breakthrough
themes.description: Xi Jinping's Sep 24-25 visit — his first to the White House in 11 years — yielded tariff cuts on roughly $30B of goods (agriculture, seafood, medical devices, small appliances and toys), a new bilateral trade committee, and an extended truce. But the two governments couldn't agree on what was even discussed regarding rare earths: the US fact sheet cited a weaker commitment from Beijing to 'address concerns' over specific element shortages, while China's official 8-point readout dropped the topic entirely. The underlying April 2025 export-licensing regime is untouched, and Washington's earlier demand that China dismantle it has quietly disappeared from the conversation — a reset of expectations, not a resolution.

themes.tag: BEIJING KEEPS THE TAP DELIBERATELY SLOW
themes.title: Export data shows China tightening, not loosening, heading into the summit
themes.description: Chinese rare-earth magnet shipments to the US fell to 512 tonnes in August — down 20% month-over-month and 13% year-over-year — even as diplomatic hopes built. Capital Economics reads this as Beijing 'testing the limits of the truce' by keeping licence approvals slow and selective, layered on top of Chinese suppliers who are independently refusing some shipments for fear of domestic retaliation. The leverage China demonstrated all summer didn't get negotiated away in Washington; if anything, the data suggests it was reinforced right before the meeting.

themes.title: Vertical-integration deals and groundbreaks proceed on their own timeline
themes.description: Away from the summit theater, the mine-to-magnet buildout kept moving: Energy Fuels' $299M acquisition of Australian Strategic Materials adds a Korean metals plant, the Dubbo project, and a planned US alloy facility, creating what the companies call the largest fully integrated rare-earth producer outside China. USA Rare Earth completed its Serra Verde combination and broke ground on a $1.2B Blacksburg, SC magnet-and-metal facility. None of this depends on Beijing's mood — but all of it is multi-year construction and integration risk, not yet cash flow.

rows.angle: Largest non-China rare-earth producer (Australia/Malaysia); pushing into magnet metals
rows.watch for: Amanda Lacaze's transition-support window formally closes Sep 30 with still no permanent CEO named — Pol Le Roux remains only interim more than three months into the search. Offsetting the governance overhang: strong FY26 results on higher realized pricing, a new LS Eco Energy partnership in South Korea, and a renewed 10-year Malaysian operating license. Shares at A$14.22, Buy consensus with an A$17.93 target (26% upside)

New CEO Ragnar Udd (ex-BHP) still doesn't take the seat until Feb 1, 2027, with Eduardo Bartolomeo added to the board in July. Buy consensus with a $171.56 target (56% upside) — the biggest gap between price and target of any Tier 1 name here

rows.angle: Copper — the electrification metal at scale
rows.watch for: Copper set a fresh all-time high near $6.83/lb on Sep 22-23 as AI data-center demand, tightening mine supply, tariff-driven stockpiling and a China demand recovery converged. FCX closed at $72.31 with its market cap up 92% year-over-year to $103.8B — essentially at the Street's $72.45 average target, and the Section 232 refined-copper tariff decision that drove the Sep 10-11 selloff is still unresolved either way

A new Pasqal/Riven Systems partnership explores quantum computing for rare-earth extraction. rows.angle: Uranium + rare-earth processing at White Mesa
rows.watch for: Agreed to acquire Australian Strategic Materials for $299M, adding a Korean metals plant, the Dubbo feedstock project, and a planned US alloy facility — the companies bill it as the largest fully integrated REE producer outside China. White Mesa's heavy-rare-earth buildout continues toward 2027 commercial output. Shares at $11.35 (+0.27%), Strong Buy consensus with a $24.15 target (113% upside)

JPMorgan upgraded shares to Overweight with a $6 target, citing higher lithium price assumptions, and Motley Fool frames Thacker Pass as 'moving from a development story toward an execution story' as construction advances. Shares closed at $2.75 (-2.8%) — still Hold consensus despite a $5.61 average target (104% upside), reflecting how much of the case still rides on lithium prices and a mechanical-completion date that remains late 2027

bear_case.title: Diplomacy delivered relief, not resolution
bear_case.description: The Xi summit produced tariff cuts and a trade committee, but rare earths got weaker language than October 2025's commitments, China's own summit readout dropped the topic, and the April 2025 export-licensing regime stands untouched. Chinese magnet shipments to the US fell another 20% month-over-month in August even as the meeting approached — the leverage China holds wasn't negotiated away, and investors betting on a durable thaw are still waiting for evidence of one.

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium carbonate's bounce to $20,010/t is being read by analysts as normalization after a mid-year rally to $27,000/t that had 'outrun market fundamentals,' not a fresh bull leg. Copper's record run to $6.83/lb rests partly on tariff-driven stockpiling and an unresolved Section 232 decision that could deflate the premium as easily as it could extend it — a reminder that a producer can be an excellent business at the wrong point in its price cycle.

bear_case.title: Vertical integration means execution risk, not just geology
bear_case.description: Energy Fuels' $299M Australian Strategic Materials deal and USA Rare Earth's Serra Verde/Blacksburg buildout both require years of construction, permitting and cross-continent integration before 'mine-to-magnet' claims turn into cash flow. USAR remains down more than 50% from its 52-week high despite genuine physical progress — a reminder that the market is pricing execution risk, not just the strategic logic of the plan.

bear_case.title: Leadership and dilution overhangs are still open, not closed
bear_case.description: Lynas' Sep 30 transition-support deadline arrives with Pol Le Roux still only interim CEO after more than three months; Albemarle's incoming CEO doesn't start until February 2027; and USA Rare Earth keeps layering new securities issuance on top of its Serra Verde stock deal. None of these is disqualifying alone, but none has actually resolved either.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: The Xi summit's 'relief without resolution' outcome left the DoD/Apple-anchored thesis unchanged either way — China's own summit readout omitted rare earths, and shares closed Sep 25 at $48.83, still 31% off August's high. Sizing up to become the sector's sole senior Core position now that Freeport has moved to Watch on a fully-priced copper rally; this is a reallocation, not new bullish news on MP itself. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Copper's fresh record near $6.83/lb pushed FCX's market cap up 92% year-over-year to $103.8B, but the stock now trades at $72.31 against a $72.45 average analyst target — essentially zero implied upside — with the Section 232 tariff decision that triggered the Sep 10-11 selloff still unresolved. Moving off Core to Watch: this looks like an excellent business priced for perfection at the top of a commodity cycle, not a name to keep adding at these levels.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths
positions.note: Amanda Lacaze's transition-support window formally closes Sep 30 with Pol Le Roux still only interim CEO more than three months into the search — a hard deadline arriving with no resolution. Strong FY26 pricing and a new South Korean partnership don't offset the governance uncertainty.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: Lithium carbonate's bounce to ~$20,010/t on Chinese EV restocking lifted shares to $112.92 mid-week before they gave some back to $109.73; the new CEO still doesn't start until Feb 2027, and analysts are still calling the price recovery normalization rather than a new trend — good business, still the wrong point to size up.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: The Serra Verde merger closed Sep 3 and the Blacksburg, SC groundbreak followed a week later, but shares whipsawed on Trump-Xi headlines (down 7% intraweek to $15.83) and remain more than 50% off their 52-week high. Weight held roughly flat: genuine construction progress, but dilution and event-driven volatility keep this sized as a speculative position, not a core one.

positions.name: Energy Fuels
positions.note: The $299M Australian Strategic Materials acquisition adds a Korean metals plant, the Dubbo project and a planned US alloy facility — a genuine step up in vertical-integration ambition that the companies bill as the largest fully integrated REE producer outside China. Sizing up within Speculative to reflect the upgraded strategic footprint, while multi-continent integration risk keeps this short of Core.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: JPMorgan's upgrade to Overweight ($6 target) on higher lithium price assumptions, plus this week's carbonate bounce to $20,010/t, both support the 'development to execution' framing as Thacker Pass construction advances. Sizing up modestly from the sector's smallest speculative position, though a still-Hold consensus and a late-2027 mechanical-completion date argue against going further.
